summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.10/400)

data.turoyo: <...> Bale kətwo hən msalanwo an naʕimaṯṯe, i naqqa d dəmxiwo an naʕimaṯṯe. Maḥkanwonne ḥəkkoyat basime lašan an naʕime d ṭəwʕi. <...>
data.translation: <...> But there were some who entertained their children, when the children lay down. They would tell them nice stories so that the children would fall asleep. <...>

rationale: First II Infectum-wa box; explicit child object and bedtime storytelling support existing entertainment sense 1. English is the supplied project machine translation [MT]; sense determined from Turoyo.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1b in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.15/566)

data.turoyo: <...> ʕAde, uṣul yo, əzzənwo lu ʕaza msalanwo u ʕamo. Yaʕni msalanwo more du ʕaza.
data.translation: <...> A custom, it is the practice; they would go to the mourning gathering and console the people. That is, they would console the bereaved.

rationale: First Infectum-wa example for round 1 II.1b; overt mourning and more du ʕaza resolve consolation without duplicating the sense. English is the supplied project machine translation [MT]; sense determined from Turoyo.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.18/3696)

data.translation: <...> Sweet amusement, we used to amuse one another.

rationale: New II Infectum-wa box; explicit reciprocal object ḥḏoḏe shows active entertainment, distinct from an unmarked intransitive conversation or a Detransitive. English is the supplied project machine translation [MT]; sense determined from Turoyo.

summary: New sense 1b: trösten, Trost zusprechen
rationale: Condolence formula and visits to a bereaved household establish consolation, a specialisation beyond ordinary entertainment; two verses in one account.

summary: New sense 1c: intrans. sich miteinander unterhalten, plaudern
rationale: Inclusive active msalena has joint participants and no entertained object, in an invitation to converse. One attestation; productivity remains open.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (JTM 1.2/12)

data.turoyo: Kəmmənne "ṭrowe rišayxu basimo", yaʕni kəmsalən more du miṯo.
data.translation: Sie sagen zu ihnen: Mögt ihr gesund bleiben, d.h. sie trösten die Angehörigen des Toten.

rationale: New consolation subsense; quoted condolence formula supplies Turoyo context.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (JTM 1.2/16)

data.turoyo: w gdoṯən an nošanək, gəmsalən u ahəl diḏe.
data.translation: und dass die Leute kommen werden, um seine Angehörigen zu trösten.

rationale: Second consolation example; bare family object and prospective visitors.

summary: example for sense 1c in Infectum (PrS 19/25)

data.turoyo: Azza l gaba i pire. Barṯe du malko əmmo ahla bi pire: “Təx d msalena əšmo.”
data.translation: Als die Alte zur Prinzessin kam, rief diese ihr entgegen: »Willkommen, Alte! komm, lass uns ein wenig plaudern«.

rationale: New active intransitive conversation subsense, in an inclusive invitation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (49/22)

data.turoyo: Fayəš u lalyawo tamo w hənne kəmnaḏ̣fi aǧ ǧarḥayḏe w komsaləlle hul ṣafro.
data.translation: Er blieb die Nacht dort, und jene säuberten seine Wunden und unterhielten ihn, bis zum Morgen.

rationale: Thin active Infectum sense 1 cell; night-long care and entertainment of a wounded man.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (73/130)

data.turoyo: U šulṭono ze mə kobəʕ Kobəʕ kul lalyo noše. Howe noše msaləlle w dayqile w zəmrile.
data.translation: Was wünscht der Sultan? Er wünscht, daß jeden Abend Leute da sind, die ihn unterhalten und für ihn spielen und singen.

rationale: Fifth active Infectum sense 1 example; entertainment linked to music and singing.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (71/60)

data.turoyo: W fayəš kul yawmo kəzzeyo, koməštaʕe hiye w muduraṯṯe baw waroqe, misale hiye w hiye tane.
data.translation: Und jeden Tag ging er und spielte mit ihrem Vorsteher Karten, und sie unterhielten sich, jener und er, allein.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; two participants enjoying a card game, with no externally entertained patient.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: sich trösten; sich unterhalten, sich zerstreuen
rationale: Existing 41/18 and new card-playing context 71/60 show enjoyable diversion without grief; sich trösten alone is too narrow.

summary: Active II entertains a patient marked by a suffix, often doubled with l-, or by a bare noun. Condolence contexts add bare bereaved-family objects and justify subsense 1b.

Detransitive misale expresses self-directed comfort or shared diversion, rather than being entertained by an external agent. B ṣurtəx supplies the source of comfort in PrS 5/26; the participants are coordinated in the card-game context.
The inclusive active conversation invitation differs from Detransitive in its overt form; its constructional status is retained provisionally, without asserting a productive new paradigm.
The condolence formula ṭrowe rišayxu basimo identifies the social act but contains no occurrence of sly; it is not a new verb idiom. No other new fixed collocation is established.
Round 2 is based on the supplied Jan Turoyo; accompanying English is project machine translation [MT]. Round 1 was read first and its proposals are not duplicated.
Jan adds the II Infectum-wa box for entertainment and for round 1 consolation 1b. The same msalanwo morphology occurs with children, the bereaved and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe.
The reciprocal object in Jan 2.18/3696 keeps active II.1: entertaining each other does not by itself instantiate round 1 intransitive chatting 1c or Detransitive misale.
Tasliya in Jan 2.18/3696 is a cognate Arabic-related entertainment noun alongside a full verb, not a light-verb construction. No additional idiom is established.

The supplied local passage does not identify the consolers as women; gender and role from a larger reader context are not independently adopted. Likewise English we does not settle person in msalanwo.
Is active msalena 'let us chat' productive across persons and contexts, or mainly an inclusive invitation formula?
In 71/60, does misale imply conversation specifically or simply enjoyable company while playing cards? The gloss addition keeps the broader reading.
Reconcile PrS 5/26 with old prs 13/11 before replacing the inherited citation.
Confirm the person and gender values of msalanwo at Jan 2.18/3696 and whether the subject is inclusive speakers or other elders.
Does the explicit reciprocal construction contrast systematically with round 1 active intransitive chatting 1c and Detransitive misale? Jan alone shows a direct reciprocal object.
Jan funeral consolation directly supports round 1 active trösten with zero-marked u ʕamo rephrased as more du ʕaza. Two tokens, one passage; no new sense.
